polityNote: Russian Empire (Siberia and the Far East) to 1917-11-06 (Provisional Government from March 1917). Amur lands Russian from the Aigun treaty (1858), Ussuri lands from Peking (1860), all Sakhalin from 1875, southern Sakhalin Japanese from 1905; Uryankhai a protectorate from 1914. Old Style decree dates converted to Gregorian (+12 days in the 19th century, +13 from 1900-03-01 O.S.).

No outer change until 1917-12 (Troitskaya volost to Tatarsk uyezd, outside scope).

sources.title: Енисейская губерния — Википедия (oldid 154900457)

sources.title: Усинский пограничный округ — Википедия (oldid 148785420)

sources.title: Забайкальская область — Википедия (oldid 152486932)

sources.title: Амурская область (Российская империя) — Википедия (oldid 146240074)

spans.dateNote: Starts with the Amur oblast decree of 8 Dec 1858 O.S. (ПСЗ-2 № 33862) = 20 Dec 1858, which fixed the Transbaikal/Amur junction at the Shilka–Argun confluence. Internal re-cuts 1870 (Barguzin, Selenga) and 1872 (Troitskosavsk) do not touch the outer line.

unresolved.what: Tobolsk governorate before the 1887 transfer of Yudinskaya volost
unresolved.why: Until 1887 Tyukalinsk (earlier Omsk) okrug held Yudinskaya volost, which lies inside the 1897 Kainsk uyezd atom (Tomsk group); before that Omsk oblast 1822–1838 and the 1868 loss of Omsk also moved the outer line.
unresolved.needs: Yudinskaya volost as a separate atom (1897 Kainsk uyezd split along the pre-1887 line)

unresolved.why: Tomsk lacked Yudinskaya volost (part of the Kainsk atom) before 1887; earlier also Omsk oblast 1822–1838 and the Semipalatinsk lands (1854/1856).
unresolved.needs: Yudinskaya volost as a separate atom

unresolved.what: Tomsk and Altai governorates after the split of 17 (30) June 1917
unresolved.why: The same resolution re-cut Barnaul, Kainsk, Tomsk and Mariinsk uyezds into eight (Novo-Nikolaevsk, Kamen, Slavgorod, Togur new); the Tomsk/Altai line runs inside 1897 uyezds (Novo-Nikolaevsk area of Barnaul uyezd). RISTAT’s Novo-Nikolaevsk atom is not a documented 1897 or 1917 line, so neither governorate can be written.
unresolved.needs: the 1917 temporary boundary description (annex to the resolution) as atoms

unresolved.what: Irkutsk governorate before 1851 (with Transbaikal, and Yakutsk/Okhotsk dependencies)
unresolved.why: Until 1851 the governorate also contained Verkhneudinsk and Nerchinsk okrugs, whose eastern edge was the Nerchinsk-treaty line (Gorbitsa), not the 1897 Transbaikal line.
unresolved.needs: the pre-1858 Gorbitsa–Argun strip as a separate atom

unresolved.why: Part of Irkutsk governorate to 1851; 1851–1858 the left bank of the Shilka east of the Gorbitsa was Qing under the Nerchinsk treaty until Aigun (1858) and the Amur decree, so the oblast was smaller than the 1897 atoms.
unresolved.needs: the Gorbitsa–Ust-Strelka strip as a separate atom

unresolved.what: Yakutsk oblast before the Udsky transfer
unresolved.why: Until 1856/1857 Yakutsk oblast held Okhotsk (from 1849) and Udsky okrugs, which are 1897 Primorskaya atoms; before 1851 it was under Irkutsk governorate. The dates of 1849/1851/1856/1857 could not all be fixed to the day.

unresolved.what: Amur lands before the Amur oblast
unresolved.why: Qing territory under the Nerchinsk treaty, with Russian posts from 1854; ceded by the Aigun treaty of 28 May 1858; organised as an oblast only by the decree of 20 Dec 1858.

unresolved.what: Amur oblast after the 1904 cession to Primorskaya
unresolved.why: Part of the Urmi and upper Amgun basins moved to Khabarovsk okrug in 1904; the new line runs through the 1897 Amur atom.
unresolved.needs: the 1904 Urmi/Amgun transfer area as a separate atom

unresolved.why: Kamchatka/Okhotsk units with other lines before 1856; Ussuri lands Qing until Aigun 1858 / Peking 1860; Sakhalin an undivided Russo-Japanese condominium (Shimoda 1855) to 1875, so the Primorskaya share of it has no line.
unresolved.needs: no atom set can carry the condominium

unresolved.what: Primorskaya oblast during the Vladivostok military governorate
unresolved.why: Vladivostok, the Muravyov-Amursky peninsula and Russky island formed a separate governorate inside the 1897 South Ussuri atom.
unresolved.needs: the Muravyov-Amursky peninsula + Russky island as a separate atom

unresolved.what: Sakhalin 1880–1884 (part of Primorskaya during the Vladivostok window, then separated)
unresolved.why: Belonged to Primorskaya, which cannot be drawn in this window; the day of the 1884 separation was not established (okrugs formed 15 May 1884).

unresolved.what: Primorskaya oblast after 1904 (incl. Udsky uyezd to Sakhalin oblast 1914)
unresolved.why: From 1904 the oblast held Amur lands inside the 1897 Amur atom; from 1909 it lost Kamchatka, and on 26 Feb (11 Mar) 1914 Udsky uyezd went to Sakhalin oblast, itself undrawable.
unresolved.needs: the 1904 transfer area as a separate atom

unresolved.why: Part of Primorskaya oblast, which cannot be drawn from 1904.

unresolved.what: Northern Sakhalin from the Japanese invasion (Sakhalin department; Sakhalin oblast from 1909)
unresolved.why: Occupied from July 1905; Portsmouth set the line at 50°N, which runs through the 1897 Aleksandrovsk okrug atom (most of it went to Japan), so Sakhalin oblast (1909) cannot be written.

unresolved.what: Korsakov okrug between invasion and cession
unresolved.why: Japanese military occupation before the Portsmouth ratifications were exchanged (25 Nov 1905).
checked: en.wikipedia Japanese invasion of Sakhalin oldid 1377003323

unresolved.what: Yeniseysk governorate after the Uryankhai protectorate
unresolved.why: Sources disagree whether the Uryankhai protectorate (not annexed; political affairs under the Irkutsk governor-general) became part of the governorate; its extent was never demarcated, so the governorate territory in this window is unsettled.

unresolved.what: Uryankhai krai under the Russian protectorate
unresolved.why: A protectorate, not formally annexed; whether it was part of Yeniseysk governorate is disputed, and its boundary with Mongolia was never demarcated.
